main_event_curves: Primary 10-minute signed connectivity event-study coefficients, in percentage points (pp) of the normalized ratio. Circles and bars show estimates and marginal 95% country-WCU unrestricted nonstudentized basic intervals; they are not simultaneous bands. The gray square at day -1 is the fixed reference, with no estimated interval. Points are not joined across relative days. Each signal has its own y scale and all intervals are shown. Reused control dates are normalized; original event, matched-group-by-relative-day, country-hour-weekday and year-month effects and daily dewpoint are retained. All day-zero intervals include zero; that is not equivalence. No precipitation adjustment or causal attribution.
main_technical_states: Technical census of all 910 forward-routed Tmax events per signal, spanning 151 countries. The 294 held events are outside this denominator. Insufficient observation is explicitly retained and never coded healthy. States use the 95% maintenance rule and 24-slot stable confirmation. This census precedes additional model-specific confound qualification; these are not heat-attributable outage counts or comparable global signal-quality rankings.
main_conditional_recovery: Country-sandwich Cox hazard ratios and marginal normal 95% intervals for stable recovery among events damaged at end. M1 shows HD, adjusted for event span and dewpoint. M2 shows NTRD additionally adjusted for HD on the same sample. Each panel has its own logarithmic range; every interval endpoint is retained. HR > 1 denotes faster confirmation conditional on damage. Complete-72-hour cases condition on future observation. BGP has no qualified recovery endpoints and is not estimable, not zero. AP sparse estimates remain exploratory; no country fixed effects/calendar strata or multiplicity correction. The eight numerical objects and confidence intervals exactly match independently verified current main-risk refits. Numerical agreement does not validate proportional hazards, independent censoring, unconditional resilience or causality.
